standard_prerequisites.name: Insertion of a short chord
standard_prerequisites.statement: insrt_i(m) is obtained by inserting a short chord joining the vertices i and i+1 and shifting all later vertices by two.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the operation whose two instances are compared.

standard_prerequisites.name: Knuth equivalence of matchings
standard_prerequisites.statement: Two matchings are Knuth equivalent when one is obtained from the other by a sequence of elementary Knuth transformations.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the relation the lemma establishes between the two insertions.

standard_prerequisites.name: Reduction process and elementary transformation
standard_prerequisites.statement: An elementary Knuth transformation is the local rewriting of three consecutive chords used to generate Knuth equivalence.
standard_prerequisites.use: The induction step produces such a transformation explicitly.

core_obligations: Reduce by symmetry to i <= j and argue by induction on the difference j-i, the case i = j being immediate (source line 1162).
For i < j, use the definition of the insertion to show that insrt_{i+1}(m) is Knuth equivalent to insrt_i(m) (source line 1164).
Apply the induction hypothesis to insrt_{i+1}(m) and combine the two equivalences to conclude (source line 1164).

proof_roadmap.step: Symmetry reduction and induction on the distance between the two insertion positions.
Compare consecutive insertions through the definition of insrt and close the induction.

difficulty_reason: Counted unit is the author's labelled lemma at source lines 1157-1160: for a matching m and any two insertion positions i and j, the matchings obtained by inserting a short chord at i and at j are Knuth equivalent. The proof (source lines 1161-1165) is an induction on the distance between the two positions, and its only non-formal step is the claim that inserting at i+1 is Knuth equivalent to inserting at i; that claim has to be read off the explicit vertex-shifting formula of the insertion definition rather than from the statement, and it is what makes the induction run. The statement records neither the induction parameter nor the appeal to the shifting formula.
